### `discussion_board_articles`

Core articles representing economic and political discussion topics.

This table stores the primary discussion objects that users browse,
search, read, create, edit, and delete. Each record represents one
article with its title, body, optional summary, category assignment,
moderation state, and audit timestamps.

Authorship is modeled through subtype tables {@link
discussion_board_article_of_memberusers} and {@link
discussion_board_article_of_adminusers}, allowing either a member user or
an admin user to own the article without using nullable polymorphic
foreign keys.

Articles are subject to moderation and can move between business states
such as Active, Hidden, and Deleted. Soft deletion is implemented using
the deleted_at field, while moderation_state records the current
visibility state from a business perspective.

Articles are linked to categories via {@link
discussion_board_article_categories} to support simple filtering and
navigation. Per-member like engagement is represented in {@link
discussion_board_article_likes}. Any aggregated metrics or counters for
views or likes should be implemented in separate materialized views, not
in this primary table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the article. Unique identifier for each discussion article.
- `discussion_board_article_category_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the category of this article. {@link
  > discussion_board_article_categories.id}. Each article belongs to exactly
  > one primary category.
- `title`
  > Human-readable title of the article. Must be non-empty and respect
  > minimum and maximum length constraints for article titles.
- `body`
  > Main body text of the article. Contains the full discussion content
  > written by the author and must satisfy length constraints defined for
  > article bodies.
- `summary`
  > Optional short plain-text summary of the article. Used in listings or
  > previews and limited to a small maximum length. Nullable when no summary
  > is provided.
- `moderation_state`
  > Business moderation state of the article. Expected values conceptually
  > include "Active", "Hidden", and "Deleted" to represent visibility and
  > moderation decisions. Enforcement of allowed values is handled in
  > application logic.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the article was first created. Used for sorting lists and
  > audit purposes.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent successful update to the article content or
  > metadata. Equal to created_at for never-edited articles.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the article was logically deleted from a data-retention
  > perspective. Nullable; when set, the article should be treated as Deleted
  > in business workflows and excluded from normal listings.

### `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers`

Authorship subtype linking articles to member users.

This table represents the ownership of articles created by regular member
users. Each record connects exactly one article in {@link
discussion_board_articles} with exactly one member user in {@link
discussion_board_memberusers}.

The 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype is enforced with
a unique constraint on discussion_board_article_id, ensuring that a given
article has at most one memberUser author record. Articles authored by
admins use the separate [discussion_board_article_of_adminusers](#discussion_board_article_of_adminusers)
table.

This design follows the main-entity plus subtype pattern to avoid
nullable polymorphic foreign keys and to keep ownership constraints
explicit at the database level.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the member user authorship record.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the article authored by a member user. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}. Unique to enforce a 1:1 relationship
  > between an article and this subtype row.
- `discussion_board_memberuser_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the member user who authored the article. {@link
  > discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Many articles can be authored by the
  > same member user.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this authorship link was created. Typically identical to
  > the article creation time for member-authored articles.

### `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers`

Authorship subtype linking articles to admin users.

This table represents the ownership of articles created by
administrators. Each record connects exactly one article in {@link
discussion_board_articles} with exactly one admin user in {@link
discussion_board_adminusers}.

The 1:1 relationship between an article and this subtype is enforced with
a unique constraint on discussion_board_article_id, ensuring that a given
article has at most one adminUser author record. Articles authored by
regular members use the separate {@link
discussion_board_article_of_memberusers} table.

Using this subtype avoids nullable polymorphic foreign keys, keeping
authorship constraints and relations explicit and fully normalized.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the admin user authorship record.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the article authored by an admin user. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}. Unique to enforce a 1:1 relationship
  > between an article and this subtype row.
- `discussion_board_adminuser_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the admin user who authored the article. {@link
  > discussion_board_adminusers.id}. Many articles can be authored by the
  > same admin user.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this authorship link was created. Typically identical to
  > the article creation time for admin-authored articles.

### `discussion_board_article_likes`

Per-member like engagement records for articles.

This table stores individual like actions performed by member users on
articles. Each record represents that a specific member user has liked a
specific article, with a creation timestamp for audit and ordering.

A unique composite constraint on (discussion_board_article_id,
discussion_board_memberuser_id) ensures that a member user can like a
given article at most once. Removing a like can be modeled by deleting
the corresponding row.

This structure supports queries such as whether a member has liked a
particular article, listing all likes made by a member, and aggregating
like counts per article. Only member users can like articles; admin users
can moderate content but do not require separate like ownership modeling.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the article like record.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the liked article. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}. Many likes can reference the same article.
- `discussion_board_memberuser_id`
  > Foreign key referencing the member user who liked the article. {@link
  > discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Many likes can be created by the same
  > member user.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the like was created. Used for audit trails and ordering
  > of engagement activity.

### `discussion_board_comments`

Top-level text comments attached directly to discussion board articles.

This model stores the core business data for each comment, including its
article relationship, text body, author type discriminator, moderation
status, and lifecycle timestamps.

Each comment belongs to exactly one article and is authored either by a
member user or an admin user via the polymorphic ownership pattern. The
concrete author relationship details are held in the subsidiary tables
[discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers](#discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers) and {@link
discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers}.

Moderation uses a simple status field (for example, Active, Hidden,
Deleted) together with soft deletion to control visibility in lists and
article views while preserving auditability for administrators.

Properties as follows:

- `id`
  > Primary key of the comment. Uniquely identifies a discussion comment
  > record.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Foreign key to the article this comment belongs to. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}. The comment is always attached to a
  > single, existing article.
- `author_type`
  > Logical type of the comment author. Expected values include "member" for
  > member users and "admin" for admin users. Used for quick filtering and
  > must be consistent with the corresponding ownership subtype table entry.
- `body`
  > Text content of the comment. Must be non-empty and within
  > business-defined length limits (for example, up to 5,000 visible
  > characters).
- `status`
  > Business-level moderation status of the comment. Typical values:
  > "Active", "Hidden", or "Deleted". Controls visibility to regular users
  > while allowing administrators to review handled content.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was created. Used for ordering and audit
  > trails.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the comment was last updated. Updated whenever the body or
  > moderation-related fields change.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates that the comment is
  > logically deleted and should be excluded from normal user views while
  > still remaining in storage for audit or recovery purposes.

### `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers`

Ownership subtype entity that links a comment to its member user author
and the creating session.

This model implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comments
authored by regular member users. Each row represents a 1:1 extension of
[discussion_board_comments](#discussion_board_comments) for comments whose actor type is a
member user.

It records the member account that authored the comment, the session
context at creation time, and a timestamp, allowing precise audit of
which member and which session produced the comment without nullable
foreign keys on the main comment table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the member user comment ownership record.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`
  > Foreign key to the base comment entity. {@link
  > discussion_board_comments.id}. Enforced as unique to ensure a strict 1:1
  > relationship for member-authored comments.
- `discussion_board_memberuser_id`
  > Foreign key to the member user account that authored the comment. {@link
  > discussion_board_memberusers.id}. Always required for member-authored
  > comments.
- `discussion_board_memberuser_session_id`
  > Foreign key to the member user session associated with the comment
  > creation. [discussion_board_memberuser_sessions.id](#discussion_board_memberuser_sessions). Captures
  > connection context such as IP and referrer at creation time.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this ownership record was created. Typically matches the
  > creation time of the underlying comment and is used for audit and
  > traceability.

### `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`

Ownership subtype entity that links a comment to its admin user author
and the creating session.

This model implements the polymorphic ownership pattern for comments
authored by admin users. Each row represents a 1:1 extension of {@link
discussion_board_comments} for comments whose actor type is an
administrator.

It records the admin account that authored the comment, the session
context at creation time, and a timestamp so that administrative
commentary can be audited separately from member commentary without
nullable foreign keys on the main comment table.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the admin user comment ownership record.

### `discussion_board_attachments`

File attachments associated with discussion board articles.

This table stores metadata for images and documents that are attached to
individual articles in the economic/political discussion board. Each row
represents a single file that belongs to exactly one article, and the
attachment has no lifecycle independent of its parent article.

The model records user-visible filename, MIME-like content type, file
size, a display order within the parent article, and a URI pointing to
the stored object. It also tracks a simple moderation status that aligns
with article/content states such as Active, Hidden, and Deleted, as well
as standard temporal audit fields.

Attachments are always managed through article operations or
administration tools and are not directly searchable as a standalone
resource for end users. They follow the visibility of their parent
article while allowing administrators to hide or delete individual files
when necessary.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key. Unique identifier for the attachment record.
- `discussion_board_article_id`
  > Parent article that this attachment belongs to. {@link
  > discussion_board_articles.id}.
- `file_uri`
  > URI location of the stored file object. Used by the application to
  > retrieve or stream the attachment content.
- `file_name`
  > Original or user-visible file name of the attachment. May be normalized
  > for safety while remaining recognizable to users.
- `content_type`
  > MIME-like content type of the attachment, such as "image/jpeg" or
  > "application/pdf". Used to decide preview vs download behavior.
- `file_size`
  > Size of the attachment file in bytes. Used for enforcing per-file and
  > per-article size limits and for displaying approximate size to users.
- `order_in_article`
  > Display order index of this attachment within its parent article. Lower
  > values are shown earlier in attachment lists.
- `status`
  > Moderation and lifecycle status of the attachment. Typical values mirror
  > content states such as "active", "hidden", or "deleted" as defined by
  > business rules.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the attachment record was created. Represents the time the
  > file was first associated with the article.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the attachment record was last updated. Updated whenever
  > metadata or status changes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp. When set, indicates the attachment is considered
  > deleted for business purposes even if metadata is retained internally.

### `discussion_board_reports`

Central entity representing a single user report about an article,
comment, or attachment.

Each row captures the reporting user type, target content type, reason
category, optional free-text explanation, and the current moderation
status and action chosen by administrators.

Moderation workflows use this table as the primary queue for reviewing
reported content, changing statuses from submitted through in_review to
resolved, and applying actions such as keeping, hiding, deleting content,
or restricting the owning member user.

Reports are append-only audit records; they are not soft-deleted, and
their lifecycle is independent from the lifecycle of the underlying
content or reporting account.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the report. Uniquely identifies a single report instance.
- `target_type`
  > Discriminator describing which type of content this report targets.
  > Typical values are "article", "comment", or "attachment" and are enforced
  > at the application layer.
- `reporter_type`
  > Discriminator describing which actor type submitted the report. Typical
  > values are "memberuser" or "adminuser" and are enforced at the
  > application layer.
- `reason_code`
  > Machine-friendly code representing the primary reason category for this
  > report. Example values include "hate_abuse", "harassment", "spam",
  > "off_topic", "dangerous_misleading", and "other". Validation for allowed
  > values is handled in the application.
- `description`
  > Optional free-text explanation provided by the reporter to clarify the
  > reason. Required by business rules when reason_code is "other", but
  > stored as nullable at schema level.
- `status`
  > Current workflow status of the report. Typical values are "submitted",
  > "in_review", or "resolved". Used to drive admin report queues and
  > filtering.
- `action`
  > Administrative decision applied in response to this report. Example
  > values include "none", "keep", "hide_content", "delete_content", and
  > "restrict_user". Business rules determine valid combinations with status.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the report was created and submitted by the reporting user.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the report was last updated, typically when an admin
  > changes status or action.

### `discussion_board_memberuser_notification_preferences`

Notification preference settings for a single member user account.

Stores per-member configuration flags controlling which categories of
notifications the system is allowed to send, such as activity on the
user’s own content, digest summaries, and optional marketing or
non-essential announcements.

Each record is strictly associated with exactly one {@link
discussion_board_memberusers} row, forming a 1:1 relationship so that
every member user can have at most one preference set.

Business logic uses these flags at send time to decide whether to deliver
a notification, while mandatory service announcements remain governed by
global policy rather than stored preferences.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key of the member user notification preferences record.
- `discussion_board_memberuser_id`
  > Owner member user account whose notification preferences are stored in
  > this row. [discussion_board_memberusers.id](#discussion_board_memberusers).
- `activity_notifications_enabled`
  > Indicates whether the member user wishes to receive notifications about
  > activity on their own content, such as replies to their articles or
  > comments.
- `digest_notifications_enabled`
  > Indicates whether the member user wishes to receive periodic digest or
  > summary notifications that aggregate recent relevant activity.
- `marketing_notifications_enabled`
  > Indicates whether the member user allows optional marketing-style or
  > non-essential announcement notifications, separate from mandatory service
  > announcements.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was first
  > created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp recording when this notification preference record was last
  > updated.

### `discussion_board_adminuser_notification_preferences`

Notification preference settings for a single admin user account.

Stores per-admin configuration flags controlling which categories of
notifications the system is allowed to send, such as notifications about
activity on the admin’s own content, digest summaries, and optional
marketing or non-essential announcements.

Each record is strictly associated with exactly one {@link
discussion_board_adminusers} row, forming a 1:1 relationship so that
every admin user can have at most one preference set.

While administrators must still receive mandatory service and policy
communications, these flags allow fine-tuning of non-essential categories
and reduce noise for operational accounts.

operations.specification: Create a guest join endpoint for the discussion_board_guestusers table. This operation will create (or reuse, depending on business rules) a minimal guest placeholder account using an opaque anonymous_token, and then issue JWT access/refresh tokens for the guestUser actor. The path will be /auth/guestUser/join with POST method. Request body will carry whatever fingerprint or client-side identifier is needed to derive or propose anonymous_token; response body will be a standard authorized payload DTO for DiscussionBoardGuestUser. This endpoint is public (no prior auth) and uses authorizationType "join" and authorizationActor "guestUser".
operations.description:
This API operation registers or materializes a guest user placeholder account in the discussion board system based on the Prisma table discussion_board_guestusers.

The underlying discussion_board_guestusers table has an id primary key of type uuid that uniquely identifies each guest user placeholder record. The core business identifier stored for a guest is anonymous_token, a non-null string that serves as an opaque token or fingerprint to correlate the same unauthenticated visitor across visits. The schema enforces a unique index on anonymous_token so that the same token cannot map to multiple guest rows, which allows this endpoint to either create a new record or reuse an existing one when the same token is presented.

The table also has created_at and updated_at datetime fields that capture when the guest record was created and last updated. These timestamps must be maintained consistently whenever a new guest is created or when an existing guest record is touched as part of join processing. Additionally, there is a nullable deleted_at field that marks when a guest record has been closed or is no longer in active use. When deleted_at is not null, the system should treat the guest as inactive and either create a new record or restore the existing one according to business policy.

From a security perspective, this endpoint does not collect passwords or personally identifiable information. It instead relies on the opaque anonymous_token to represent the guest identity and then issues JWT tokens for the guestUser actor role. The token payload will internally reference the discussion_board_guestusers.id value so the backend can later resolve guest-specific state if needed, while still keeping the external interface minimal.

Validation rules should ensure that anonymous_token is a non-empty string that meets any length or pattern constraints defined at the DTO level, and that a single active guest record exists per token, in line with the unique index on anonymous_token. If an existing record is found with a non-null deleted_at timestamp, the implementation should either reject the join or clear deleted_at and update updated_at, depending on defined business rules.

This operation is typically the first step for guests that need a persistent identity for features like tracking read history or later conversion to a full member account. It works together with the guest token refresh endpoint, which uses the guest's refresh token to get a new access token without changing the underlying discussion_board_guestusers record.
operations.summary: Register or materialize a guest placeholder account in discussion_board_guestusers and issue JWT tokens for guestUser.

requestBody.description: Guest join payload containing the opaque token or fingerprint used to derive or look up anonymous_token in discussion_board_guestusers.

responseBody.description: Authorized guestUser session information including issued JWT tokens derived from discussion_board_guestusers.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Create a guest refresh endpoint for the discussion_board_guestusers table. This operation will validate a guest refresh token associated with a specific discussion_board_guestusers.id and then issue a new set of JWT access (and potentially refresh) tokens for the guestUser actor. The path will be /auth/guestUser/refresh with POST method. Request body will contain the refresh token and any required client context; response body will be the standard DiscussionBoardGuestUser authorized DTO. This endpoint is accessible with a valid refresh token, uses authorizationType "refresh", and authorizationActor "guestUser".
operations.description:
This API operation refreshes JWT tokens for a guestUser actor that is backed by a record in the discussion_board_guestusers table.

The discussion_board_guestusers table defines id as the uuid primary key for each guest placeholder account. It also stores anonymous_token as an opaque string used to correlate visits from the same unauthenticated visitor, with a unique index on anonymous_token to prevent conflicting identities. While anonymous_token is the primary business key at creation time, the refresh endpoint typically relies on the subject embedded in the refresh token, which should reference the id field so the system can reliably look up the correct guest record.

The table contains created_at and updated_at datetime fields that record when the guest entry was created and when it was last updated. Because category administration affects the classification of content across the entire board, this endpoint must be restricted to administrative actors in the `discussionBoard_adminusers` domain; normal member users cannot define categories.

This response is suitable for immediate use in admin UIs that need to display the new category or navigate to its detail page. Because modifying categories is a privileged operation that affects how all users experience the board, this endpoint is restricted to administrative actors and should be protected by appropriate authentication and authorization mechanisms mapped from the `authorizationActors: ["adminUser"]` declaration.

All validation and error handling should be consistent with the Prisma schema constraints, especially the uniqueness of `code` and non-nullability of required columns.
operations.description:
Update an existing article category in the discussion board’s master data using its business `code` as the stable identifier.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model, which stores master category definitions such as "Economy" or "Politics". Each row has a UUID primary key `id` and a machine-friendly `code` that is constrained to be unique across the system, as well as user-facing fields like `name`, an optional longer `description`, an integer `order` for display sorting, and timestamps `created_at`, `updated_at`, and an optional `deleted_at` used to indicate logical retirement. When a client issues a PUT request to `/discussionBoard/adminUser/articleCategories/{categoryCode}`, the service must resolve `categoryCode` against the `code` column, ensuring that the correct category row is selected without exposing internal UUIDs.

From a security and permission perspective, this endpoint is intended for administrative tooling where authorized admin users manage which topics are available on the economic and political discussion board. Regular member or guest users should not be allowed to modify categories, because the schema description clearly states that categories are managed by administrators rather than end users. The implementation behind this endpoint should therefore be protected so that only actors with administrative privileges—represented here by the `adminUser` authorization actor—can successfully call it. Attempts by unauthorized users must result in appropriate authorization errors before any database modification occurs.

With respect to the underlying database behavior, the update logic should respect the constraints and indexes defined on the `discussion_board_article_categories` table. The `code` must remain unique; if the API allows `code` to be changed via `IDiscussionBoardArticleCategory.IUpdate`, the service must check for conflicts and return a clear validation error when a duplicate would be created. The `order` field should be validated as a reasonable integer used for display ordering, potentially in combination with `created_at` as indicated by the composite index on `(order, created_at)`. The `updated_at` column must always be refreshed to the current timestamp whenever any editable field changes so that administrative tools can track the last modification time.

Error handling should cover several expected scenarios. If no category exists for the provided `categoryCode`, the service must return a not-found response rather than silently creating a new record, because the operation is semantically an update, not an upsert. If the category has a non-null `deleted_at` timestamp and business rules consider such categories retired, the implementation should either block updates with a clear message or, if reactivation is supported, treat this as a controlled restoration path while documenting that behavior in the implementation. This update endpoint is typically used together with a list or search endpoint such as `PATCH /articleCategories` for finding categories and a creation endpoint like `POST /articleCategories` for registering new master data entries.

The Prisma schema includes a nullable `deleted_at` column annotated as a indicator for when the category was retired, as well as `created_at` and `updated_at` timestamps. Given that description, the preferred implementation is to set `deleted_at` to the current timestamp instead of physically dropping the row, ensuring that existing foreign key relationships from `discussion_board_articles` remain valid while preventing the category from appearing in user-facing selection lists. The endpoint itself, however, is described as a DELETE operation, and the exact semantics—logical retirement versus hard deletion—must align with agreed business rules and be implemented consistently in repository logic.

This endpoint belongs to the `discussionBoard` service and operates directly on the `discussion_board_article_categories` model, whose role is to supply normalized category master data for browsing, filtering, and reporting across the board. Because categories are used widely, the delete behavior must consider constraints and indexes (such as the unique `code` and the `(order, created_at)` index) but more importantly must ensure that clients and administrative tools handle retired categories predictably, for example by excluding rows where `deleted_at` is non-null from standard list queries.
operations.description:
Remove an article category from the discussion board’s master data using its business `code` as identifier.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_article_categories` Prisma model and is exposed as `DELETE /articleCategories/{categoryCode}`. The model stores category definitions such as "Economy" or "Politics" with fields including a UUID `id`, a unique `code`, a user-facing `name`, optional `description`, an integer `order` for display ordering, and timestamps `created_at`, `updated_at`, and a nullable `deleted_at`. When this endpoint is called, the implementation must resolve the provided `categoryCode` to the corresponding row via the unique `code` column and then apply the configured deletion strategy, which typically involves marking the row as retired using `deleted_at` so that articles can continue to reference the same category record for historical integrity.

From an authorization perspective, the schema commentary clearly states that categories are managed by administrators rather than end users. Therefore, only administrative actors—represented here by the `adminUser` authorization actor—are allowed to call this endpoint. Member and guest users must not have access to this operation. The controller and service layer must enforce these permissions before any mutation occurs, returning appropriate authorization errors for callers without sufficient privileges.

The business logic behind this endpoint must take into account how removal of categories affects existing data and UI behavior. If the system uses `deleted_at` as a retirement marker, list and search operations for categories should typically filter out rows where `deleted_at` is non-null, thereby preventing retired categories from being used for new article assignments while still allowing reporting and historical queries that include them. If a truly permanent delete is configured instead, the implementation must ensure referential integrity with `discussion_board_articles` and any other dependent tables, potentially blocking deletion when active references exist. Error handling should cover not-found situations when no category matches the given `categoryCode`, and should return clear messages rather than silently succeeding. This operation is associated primarily with the `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` Prisma table, which acts as a subsidiary authorship subtype for `discussion_board_articles`, and secondarily with the `discussion_board_memberusers` table that stores the member account profile.

The endpoint exposes a read-only view that, given an `articleId` identifying a record in `discussion_board_articles`, looks up the corresponding authorship record in `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` (if the article was created by a member user rather than an admin). Using that authorship record, it then joins to the `discussion_board_memberusers` table to return a DTO representing the member author information. The response focuses on author identity and profile fields appropriate to display as "article writer" information in the UI, not on article content itself.

This operation does not perform any modification of article or user data. It is a simple retrieval and therefore uses HTTP GET semantics with no request body. It should be implemented to cleanly handle the case where the target article either does not exist, or exists but was authored by an admin user instead of a member user, in which case an appropriate not-found error for the member author context should be returned.

Retrieve information about the member user who authored a particular discussion board article.

This operation is designed for cases where articles on the economic and political discussion board are written by registered member users stored in the `discussion_board_memberusers` table, and the authorship relationship is recorded in the `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` subsidiary table. The client supplies an `articleId` path parameter, which corresponds to the primary key of a row in `discussion_board_articles`. Using this identifier, the backend looks up an authorship link record in `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` and, from there, loads the associated member user account.

From a security and privacy standpoint, the response should contain only those member profile fields that are intended to be publicly visible as author information, such as display name, optional profile metadata allowed by the business rules, and any badge or status flags that are considered safe to expose. Sensitive data like authentication credentials, internal moderation flags that are not meant for general users, or contact details that are not part of the public profile must not be included in the DTO. The operation itself is read-only and can typically be exposed to all actors, because it only reveals author information that would already be visible wherever the article is displayed.

In terms of database relationships, this operation depends on a valid `discussion_board_articles` record and an associated `discussion_board_article_of_memberusers` record for the given article. If the article was instead authored by an admin user, its authorship will be represented in `discussion_board_article_of_adminusers` and this member-author endpoint should respond as if no member author exists for that article. Implementations should therefore distinguish between the following error scenarios: the article does not exist at all, the article exists but has no member authorship record, or the article has been removed according to content removal rules. Appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages should allow clients to understand why member author information is unavailable, while not leaking unnecessary internal details.

This endpoint will commonly be used alongside other article-related operations, such as retrieving article details (`GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}`) and listing comments or attachments associated with the same article. Clients may first fetch the article, and then call this endpoint to render a dedicated author panel that specifically reflects the member user who created it when applicable.

This operation retrieves the current like engagement state for a specific discussion board article based on the underlying `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma model. It is designed to answer the question "has the current member already liked this article, and what is the current like count?" in a single, efficient call.

The operation targets records in the `discussion_board_article_likes` table, which represents per-member like engagement for articles in the economic and political discussion board. Each row in that table typically links a `discussion_board_memberusers` record to a `discussion_board_articles` record, reflecting that a particular member has expressed a like for that article. The aggregate like count for an article may be derived either by counting rows in this table for the article, or by a dedicated counter field on the article itself; this operation is responsible for exposing that information at the API layer, not for defining the storage strategy.

From a business perspective, this API is used by clients when rendering an article detail view or an article list card, so that they can display both the total number of likes and whether the currently authenticated member has already liked the article. If the requester is not authenticated as a member user, the operation still returns the article's like count while indicating that there is no member-specific like state. The article is identified by its UUID-based `articleId` path parameter, which corresponds directly to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` table.

The operation is read-only and does not modify any state in `discussion_board_article_likes` or related tables. It simply combines per-article aggregation from `discussion_board_article_likes` with article metadata from `discussion_board_articles`, and optionally the current member's like record, into a single DTO defined as `IDiscussionBoardArticleLike`. This DTO is expected to include fields such as the article identifier, total like count, and a boolean indicating whether the current member has liked the article.

The primary consumers of this endpoint are authenticated member users browsing the board, but the endpoint is also safe for public access if the service chooses to expose like counts publicly. Authorization is therefore modeled using the `memberUser` actor, leaving finer-grained role and visibility checks to downstream business logic and middleware.
operations.description:
Retrieve the like engagement state and count for a single discussion board article.

This operation reads from the `discussion_board_article_likes` Prisma table, which stores per-member like records for articles, and from the `discussion_board_articles` table, which stores the core article metadata such as identifiers, titles, and category references. For the article identified by the `articleId` path parameter, the system computes the total number of active like records associated with that article and determines whether the current authenticated member user has a corresponding like entry.

In typical schema designs, `discussion_board_article_likes` will contain foreign keys referencing `discussion_board_articles` and `discussion_board_memberusers`, along with timestamp fields for when the like was created. This endpoint can be used for "articles I liked" sections in the UI, profile pages, or analytics screens.

Typical filters include article category (via discussion_board_article_category_id), moderation_state constraints (such as only "Active" articles), and text search over title or body (supported by GIN indexes on these fields). Pagination parameters allow the client to scroll through liked articles in a stable order (for example, sorted by article created_at or by like created_at, depending on how IDiscussionBoardArticle.IRequest is designed). The memberUserId path parameter may represent either the current member viewing their own likes or another member whose public liked-articles list is being inspected, depending on business rules about profile visibility. The controller is responsible for enforcing whether a member can view another member's liked articles, using account_status and other profile fields from discussion_board_memberusers as needed. The request body uses the IDiscussionBoardComment.IRequest DTO to carry pagination parameters (such as page index and page size), sorting options (for example, sort by created_at ascending to show oldest first or descending for newest first), and optional search criteria like text search against the body column. Internally, the core comment data is stored in the `discussion_board_comments` table, which contains fields such as the textual content, timestamps created by the database or application layer, and any structural relationships like parent comment references if nested discussions are supported. The request body is represented by the `IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate` DTO, which encapsulates only the fields that clients are allowed to set, such as comment content and, when supported, a parent comment identifier for replies. Fields that are system-managed—such as primary keys, creation timestamps, and foreign keys to the article and author—are populated by the service based on the path parameter and the authenticated user context rather than being supplied directly by the caller.

In addition to the base comment entity, the system uses ownership subtype tables such as `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` to capture which actor wrote the comment and, if modeled in the schema, which login session was used at creation time. The service inspects the authenticated principal to determine whether the comment should be linked through the member or admin subtype and creates the corresponding row accordingly, respecting any unique or foreign key constraints defined in those Prisma models.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated actors, modeled here through the `authorizationActors` array indicating that both member and admin roles are valid. The article is identified using the `articleId` path parameter, which maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` Prisma model. Before inserting the comment, the system must verify that the referenced article exists and that its current status permits additional comments, following any business rules and Prisma schema comments associated with the article entity, such as flags for comment locking or archival.

Internally, the core comment data is stored in the `discussion_board_comments` table, which contains fields such as the textual content, timestamps created by the database or application layer, and any structural relationships like parent comment references if nested discussions are supported. The request body is represented by the `IDiscussionBoardComment.ICreate` DTO, which encapsulates only the fields that clients are allowed to set, such as comment content and, when supported, a parent comment identifier for replies. Fields that are system-managed—such as primary keys, creation timestamps, and foreign keys to the article and author—are populated by the service based on the path parameter and the authenticated user context rather than being supplied directly by the caller.

In addition to the base comment entity, the system uses ownership subtype tables such as `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` to capture which actor wrote the comment and, if modeled in the schema, which login session was used at creation time. The service inspects the authenticated principal to determine whether the comment should be linked through the member or admin subtype and creates the corresponding row accordingly, respecting any unique or foreign key constraints defined in those Prisma models.

Security-wise, this endpoint is restricted to authenticated actors, modeled here through the `authorizationActors` array indicating that both member and admin roles are valid. It primarily manipulates the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model and, depending on ownership and auditing design, may reference `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` to verify the author and enforce permission rules.

The comment to update is uniquely identified by the combination of the `articleId` and `commentId` path parameters. The `articleId` parameter maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` table and is used to ensure that the specified comment actually belongs to the given article, preventing cross-article tampering. The `commentId` parameter maps to the primary key of the `discussion_board_comments` table. When the request arrives, the service first loads the existing comment row and validates that both identifiers match the stored foreign key relationships.

The request body uses the `IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate` DTO, which reflects the updatable fields of the `discussion_board_comments` table—typically the textual content and possibly some flags such as whether the comment is marked as edited. System-managed fields like identifiers, creation timestamps, and article association are not directly writable and must not be altered by the client. The service logic enforces these constraints by only mapping allowed fields from the DTO to the underlying Prisma update operation.

Authorization and ownership enforcement are central to this operation. The service checks whether the authenticated actor is the original author of the comment (by inspecting ownership information from `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` or `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`) or an administrator with elevated moderation permissions. Requirements and Prisma schema comments for related restriction models, such as `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions`, must be consulted to ensure that restricted members cannot edit their comments and that admins follow the moderation policy for editing other users’ content.

On success, the operation returns an updated `IDiscussionBoardComment` DTO that contains the latest state of the comment, reflecting all changes applied through the update. This enables clients to immediately refresh their user interface without requiring an additional fetch call. If either the article or comment cannot be found, a 404 error is returned. If the authenticated user lacks permission to modify the comment, the service responds with a suitable 403 status, and validation failures in the request body yield 400-level responses with detailed error messages.
operations.description:
Update an existing comment that belongs to a specific discussion board article.

This operation enables an authenticated user—either the original member author or a privileged administrator—to modify the content of a comment that has previously been created on a discussion board article. The target comment is located using the `articleId` and `commentId` path parameters, which map respectively to the primary key of the `discussion_board_articles` model and the primary key of the `discussion_board_comments` model. By requiring both identifiers, the API ensures that the comment being updated is indeed associated with the specified article, protecting against accidental or malicious updates across article boundaries.

The request body is represented by the `IDiscussionBoardComment.IUpdate` DTO, which corresponds to the subset of `discussion_board_comments` fields that are allowed to change after creation. In most cases this will include the textual content of the comment and potentially an `edited` flag or similar metadata, while immutable fields like the comment’s identifier, original creation timestamp, and foreign keys to the article and author remain untouched. The service maps only these permitted fields to the underlying Prisma update on the `discussion_board_comments` table, thereby honoring the schema’s non-null and length constraints as described in its comments.

Ownership and permission checks are enforced using the ownership subtype tables `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`, along with any restriction information from `discussion_board_memberuser_restrictions`. For member-authored comments, the service verifies that the current authenticated member user matches the owner recorded in the corresponding subtype row and that the account is not currently restricted from editing content. For administrator-authored comments, or when admins are allowed to edit member comments for moderation purposes, the service ensures that the authenticated admin user has appropriate privileges according to the moderation rules defined in the requirements and schema documentation.

The endpoint is secured for authenticated actors only, with `authorizationActors` indicating that both member and admin roles may access it, though their effective permissions differ according to business rules. On success, the API returns the updated `IDiscussionBoardComment` DTO reflecting the latest persisted state, allowing clients to update the displayed comment in place. Error responses include 404 when either the article or comment cannot be found, 403 for insufficient permissions or restrictions, and 400-level responses for invalid update payloads—such as content that violates length limits or other validation rules derived from the Prisma schema comments.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently deletes a specific top-level text comment from a discussion board article. It operates primarily on the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model, which stores the core comment content, timestamps, and association to an article, while also implicitly relying on the ownership subtype models `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers` for authorization and auditing.

The endpoint accepts two path parameters: `articleId`, identifying the parent article record in the `discussion_board_articles` table, and `commentId`, identifying the target comment record in `discussion_board_comments`. Using both identifiers ensures that the comment being deleted is correctly scoped to the expected article and helps prevent accidental deletion of a comment attached to a different article.

From a business perspective, this deletion is intended for cases where a comment must be removed due to user request, policy violations, or administrative moderation actions. The implementation must ensure that only authorized actors—typically the comment owner (derived from the corresponding ownership subtype record) or an administrator—are allowed to perform the deletion. The underlying database operation removes the comment row and any dependent ownership subtype rows referencing it, following referential integrity rules defined in the Prisma schema.

This delete operation is logically related to other comment operations such as listing comments for an article (PATCH /articles/{articleId}/comments), retrieving a specific comment, and creating or updating comments. Clients should use this endpoint after they have identified the specific comment to remove, usually via one of the listing or detail retrieval operations.
operations.description:
Delete a specific comment associated with a discussion board article by its comment identifier within the context of its parent article.

This operation targets the `discussion_board_comments` Prisma model, which represents top-level text comments directly attached to discussion board articles. Each comment belongs to one article and is linked through a foreign key relationship to the `discussion_board_articles` table. The `articleId` path parameter identifies the parent article record, while the `commentId` path parameter identifies the specific comment row to be removed.

Authorization and ownership are determined by related subtype entities such as `discussion_board_comment_of_memberusers` and `discussion_board_comment_of_adminusers`, which link a comment to its authoring user and creation session. The provider logic must enforce that only the author of the comment or an administrator with appropriate privileges can invoke this deletion successfully. Attempts by other users should result in an authorization error response, and the implementation should avoid leaking information about comments the caller is not allowed to see.

The deletion behavior is a hard delete of the comment record and any dependent subtype records. Once deleted, the comment will no longer appear in article comment lists, and attempts to access it by `commentId` should result in a not-found response. Any associated reports, moderation records, or audit trails are expected to be handled by related tables and logic, but they are not directly manipulated by this endpoint.

This endpoint relies on the existence of the article and comment; if either the `articleId` does not correspond to a current article, or the `commentId` does not represent a comment attached to that article, the implementation should respond with a not-found error. Clients typically call this endpoint after retrieving or listing comments via companion operations such as listing comments for an article or viewing comment details.

This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of file attachments associated with a specific discussion board article. It is based on the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model, which stores attachment metadata such as filename, MIME type, size, storage URI, and the foreign key linking each attachment to its parent article in the `discussion_board_articles` table.

The endpoint is designed as a PATCH operation on `/articles/{articleId}/attachments` to support complex querying of attachments, including pagination, sorting, and optional filters (for example by file type, upload date, or uploader). The `articleId` path parameter identifies the parent article whose attachments are being queried. The request body uses the `IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest` DTO to express search criteria and pagination options, while the response body returns a paginated collection of summary attachment records via `IPageIDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary`.

This operation is read-only and does not modify any data in `discussion_board_attachments`. It is intended to power UI flows where users view or manage the list of files attached to an article prior to downloading or performing other allowed actions. Security and authorization are enforced based on the caller's ability to view the underlying article: only callers who can see the article should be allowed to list its attachments.

The operation complements other attachment-related endpoints such as uploading attachments when creating or editing an article and downloading a single attachment. Clients typically invoke this list endpoint after loading an article detail view, in order to render the associated attachments section with accurate, paginated data.

Retrieve a filtered, sorted, and paginated list of file attachments belonging to a specific discussion board article.

This operation works over the `discussion_board_attachments` Prisma model, which represents file attachments that are linked to articles in the `discussion_board_articles` table. Each attachment record stores metadata such as file name, MIME type, size, and a reference to the storage location, along with the foreign key identifying its parent article. The `articleId` path parameter specifies which article's attachments are being queried.

The request body uses the `IDiscussionBoardAttachment.IRequest` structure to capture search criteria and pagination controls. Typical fields include page index, page size, sort fields and directions, and optional filters such as file extension, content type, or uploaded-at date ranges. The endpoint returns its data as `IPageIDiscussionBoardAttachment.ISummary`, a paginated collection of lightweight attachment summary records optimized for list rendering in the UI.

This is a read-only operation: it does not modify any attachment or article data. Authorization is tied to article visibility—only users allowed to view the given article should be able to call this endpoint successfully. The implementation must also respect any access restrictions or moderation decisions that might hide certain attachments, ensuring that blocked or restricted files are not exposed in the list.

This endpoint is typically used in conjunction with article detail retrieval and individual attachment download endpoints. Clients first load the article, then use this attachments listing operation to populate an attachments section, and finally allow users to click through to download or preview specific attachments as needed.

Retrieve a single attachment record belonging to a specific discussion board article from the Prisma table discussion_board_attachments.

This GET operation is a read-only endpoint that returns metadata for one attachment row from discussion_board_attachments. The attachment is identified by its primary key id, provided as attachmentId, and is additionally scoped by the parent article’s id from discussion_board_articles, provided as articleId. This dual constraint ensures that the attachment truly belongs to the indicated article and prevents cross-article leakage.

The operation exposes the attachment’s file_uri (URI to the stored file object), file_name (user-visible filename), content_type (MIME-like media type), file_size (bytes), order_in_article (display order within the article), status (business lifecycle/moderation state), and temporal audit fields created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at as mapped in the IDiscussionBoardAttachment DTO. The underlying Prisma schema comments emphasize that attachments are subsidiary to articles and are not independently visible resources for end users.

Application logic built on this specification must respect the meaning of status and deleted_at fields. Attachments whose deleted_at is non-null, or whose status indicates hidden/deleted states, should be excluded from normal user-facing responses unless the caller is an elevated actor. The schema’s foreign key, discussion_board_article_id, must always match the articleId to consider the attachment valid for this endpoint.
operations.description:
Fetch detailed metadata for a single file attachment that belongs to a specific discussion article.

This endpoint operates on the discussion_board_attachments Prisma model, which stores attachment metadata for the discussion board. Each record in discussion_board_attachments is linked to one parent article via the discussion_board_article_id foreign key, referencing discussion_board_articles.id. The schema comments describe this table as holding information such as file_uri (location of the stored file object), file_name (original or normalized filename), content_type (for example, "image/jpeg" or "application/pdf"), file_size in bytes, order_in_article for presentation, status representing moderation and lifecycle, and audit timestamps created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at.

The path parameters enforce this relationship: articleId represents the parent article’s id from discussion_board_articles, and attachmentId represents the attachment’s id from discussion_board_attachments. The implementation must verify that the attachment row not only exists but also has its discussion_board_article_id equal to articleId, ensuring that the attachment truly belongs to that article. If either the article does not exist, the attachment is missing, or the foreign key does not match, the service must respond with a not-found style error rather than returning unrelated data.

From a business and security perspective, this operation is intended as a user-facing read of attachment metadata, not a management or administrative tool. Therefore, the implementation should honor the semantics of the status and deleted_at fields described in the schema. Records with a non-null deleted_at or with a status indicating that the attachment is hidden or deleted should not be returned to ordinary callers; instead, the operation should behave as if the attachment does not exist or is inaccessible. More privileged moderation or admin operations that can see hidden attachments would be designed separately. The response contains only metadata via IDiscussionBoardAttachment and does not stream binary content directly; clients are expected to use file_uri with the storage layer to actually download or display the file content.

Error handling must cover invalid UUID formats for articleId or attachmentId, non-existent or mismatched attachments, and any internal consistency issues with discussion_board_articles. The operation is strictly read-only and does not modify discussion_board_attachments or discussion_board_articles in any way.

A new row is inserted with a foreign key discussion_board_article_id pointing to the parent article’s id in discussion_board_articles, and with metadata fields such as file_uri, file_name, content_type, file_size, order_in_article, status, and audit timestamps.

The parent article is identified by the articleId path parameter, which maps to discussion_board_articles.id. The request body uses the IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate DTO and should provide all necessary attachment metadata except for server-managed fields like id, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. When inserting, the implementation must respect the unique index on (discussion_board_article_id, order_in_article) by validating or adjusting order_in_article so that each attachment for a given article has a distinct display order.

Because discussion_board_attachments is a subsidiary table and attachments do not have an independent lifecycle outside their articles, this operation is restricted to authenticated members who can modify the parent article. The Prisma stance for attachments (subsidiary) aligns with using this endpoint as part of article editing flows rather than as a standalone public API. Business logic must enforce constraints derived from the schema descriptions, such as size limits based on file_size, allowable content_type values, and appropriate initial status values that follow moderation rules.
operations.description:
Register a new file attachment under a specific discussion article by inserting a row into discussion_board_attachments.

This endpoint creates a child record of a discussion article in the discussion_board_attachments table. The path parameter articleId identifies the parent row in discussion_board_articles via its id. The request body must follow the IDiscussionBoardAttachment.ICreate structure, including metadata fields: file_uri (the URI where the file is already stored), file_name (user-visible filename), content_type (MIME-like type for preview or download handling), file_size (in bytes), order_in_article (which determines display sequence within the article), and status (initial moderation and lifecycle status, such as active or hidden, as defined by business rules).

On creation, the service sets discussion_board_article_id to the articleId, populates created_at and updated_at automatically to the current timestamp, and leaves deleted_at as null to indicate that the attachment is retained. The unique index (discussion_board_article_id, order_in_article) declared in the Prisma schema must be maintained: if the provided order_in_article conflicts with an existing attachment for the same article, the application should either reject the request with a validation error or adjust other attachments’ orders according to application-specific rules. Additional validation derived from the schema comments includes ensuring that file_size does not exceed configured maximum limits, that content_type belongs to an allowed whitelist (e.g., common image and document types), and that the number of attachments per article remains within non-functional requirements.

Authorization is required because discussion_board_attachments is a subsidiary model used when editing an article. This operation is exposed only to authenticated member users or administrators who have permission to update the specified article. In the Prisma-centric design, ownership and permissions are determined by related tables such as authorship subtypes on discussion_board_articles, but at the API level this is summarized as a memberUser-only endpoint with further checks in business logic. Therefore, authorizationActors is set to ["memberUser"]. Guest visitors cannot create attachments, and attempts to attach files to a non-existent, deleted, or otherwise non-editable article must result in an error response.

On success, the endpoint returns the newly created attachment row mapped to IDiscussionBoardAttachment, including its generated id, timestamps, and normalized metadata. Clients can then refresh their article editor’s attachment list or insert references to the attachment’s file_uri in the article body. Follow-up operations such as updating or logically deleting attachments, or listing all attachments for an article, would use related endpoints built on the same Prisma model.

Delete or logically retire a single attachment row from the discussion_board_attachments table that belongs to a specific article in the discussion_board_articles table, using DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}. The implementation must validate articleId and attachmentId as UUIDs and then locate a discussion_board_attachments record whose id equals attachmentId and whose discussion_board_article_id equals articleId. If no such record exists, a not-found response should be returned. The operation must respect the subsidiary stance of discussion_board_attachments by always enforcing this parent-child relationship check, ensuring that attachments are removed only in the context of their owning article.

Given that the Prisma schema for discussion_board_attachments includes a deleted_at datetime column described as a soft deletion timestamp indicating that the attachment is considered deleted for business purposes, this endpoint should typically perform a logical deletion rather than a physical row removal. That is, it should set deleted_at to the current timestamp and adjust status to a value that represents a deleted or otherwise non-active state, while keeping metadata like file_uri and file_size for internal retention or audit purposes. Clients are not required to send a request body and do not receive a response payload; they rely on HTTP status codes to infer success or failure and may subsequently refresh the article's attachment list via a separate read endpoint.
operations.description:
Delete an attachment that belongs to a specific discussion article so that it is no longer treated as an active file in the discussion board.

This endpoint is backed by the discussion_board_attachments schema, whose description explains that attachments are metadata records for files associated with discussion board articles. Each record has id as its primary key; a non-null discussion_board_article_id that references discussion_board_articles.id; and columns like file_uri, file_name, content_type, file_size, order_in_article, status, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. The schema description further notes that attachments follow the visibility of their parent article but allow administrators to hide or delete individual files when necessary, and that deleted_at is used as a soft deletion timestamp indicating business-level deletion.

When DELETE /articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} is called, the service must interpret articleId and attachmentId as UUID strings, then query for a discussion_board_attachments row matching both the given id and discussion_board_article_id. If no row matches this composite, the API should return a not-found response rather than silently ignoring the request, and it must not operate on attachments for other articles even if the attachmentId exists under a different parent. This behavior aligns with the foreign key description tying each attachment explicitly to its article.

On successful lookup, the recommended behavior is to perform a logical deletion consistent with the deleted_at column semantics: set deleted_at to the current timestamp and optionally update status to a value that reflects the deleted state. After this change, any list or detail endpoints that present attachments to end users should filter out records where deleted_at is non-null, ensuring that removed attachments no longer appear in the article's attachment list. Depending on business rules, repeated calls to delete an already-deleted attachment can either be treated as idempotent success or rejected with a conflict error if the system wants to signal that no further action is possible.

Access to this operation should be restricted to authenticated actors who are allowed to modify the content of the article, such as the member user who authored the article or an admin user performing moderation. Authorization components should therefore enforce roles for memberUser and adminUser and then delegate more granular checks (like ownership) to the domain service. Error handling must also cover invalid UUID formats, attempts to delete attachments that do not exist, and authorization failures when the caller does not have sufficient rights. Complementary operations include creating attachments for an article, updating attachment metadata via PUT on the same path, and read operations that list attachments or show attachment details while respecting deleted_at and status filtering rules defined by the discussion_board_attachments schema.

The path parameters articleId and attachmentId together identify the attachment whose related reports are to be listed.

This operation retrieves a paginated, filterable list of active or historical session records associated with a specific member user from the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions Prisma table. It serves administrative and security-oriented use cases, allowing an authorized actor to inspect where and how a given member user is currently logged in across devices or browsers.

The implementation will query the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions model constrained by the parent member user's identifier provided in the memberUserId path parameter. On top of that fixed parent condition, the request body will carry search, filtering, and pagination criteria defined by the IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.IRequest DTO, such as limiting to sessions created within certain time ranges, filtering by client information, and controlling page size and sort order. The response will return a paginated list of session summaries using the IPageIDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISummary type so that clients can display concise session rows without transferring all detailed fields.

This operation is read-only with respect to the underlying sessions; it does not create, update, or delete session entries. Its main purpose is to support features like "view all sessions for this member" pages and security dashboards, where an admin user or potentially the member themselves can review active or historical sessions and decide whether to terminate one via a separate dedicated revoke operation. Because session lifecycle management (creation, refresh, revocation) is owned by a specialized authentication subsystem, this API strictly lists sessions already recorded in the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table and must not assume control over token issuance or invalidation.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of session records belonging to a specific member user from the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table.

This endpoint operates on the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions Prisma model, which stores session data for authenticated discussion board member users. The memberUserId path parameter identifies the parent discussion_board_memberusers record whose sessions are being queried. Within that scope, the request body uses the IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.IRequest structure to specify search filters, date range constraints, sorting options, and pagination parameters so that callers can efficiently navigate a potentially large set of sessions for a single member.

From a security and authorization perspective, this operation should typically be accessible either to privileged administrative actors responsible for monitoring account activity, or to the member user themself when viewing their own account security page. The exact enforcement of whether a given caller is allowed to see another member's sessions is handled in business logic based on the authenticated principal and the memberUserId path parameter. The endpoint does not expose any sensitive secrets such as raw tokens; instead, it returns high-level session attributes suitable for display in an audit or activity log.

The response is a paginated collection of session summary objects wrapped in the IPageIDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession.ISummary DTO, which is optimized for list views and includes only the fields necessary to identify and describe sessions (for example, creation time, last activity, client device, or IP information, as defined in the schema). This operation is read-only and does not modify or terminate sessions. For revoking or invalidating sessions, separate dedicated operations must be used that interact with the underlying authentication and token infrastructure.

This endpoint is typically used after locating a particular member via user search APIs (for example, PATCH /memberUsers) or when a logged-in member navigates to a "current sessions" or "where you're logged in" page. Clients should first identify the correct memberUserId, then call this sessions listing API with appropriate search and paging criteria to display manageable subsets of the user's session history.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a specific authenticated member user's session record from the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions Prisma model. This GET operation is strictly read-only and is intended for administrative or security-audit viewing of an individual session, not for login, logout, or any other form of session lifecycle management. The endpoint uses both the parent member user identifier and the child session identifier to uniquely locate the session row, reflecting the relationship between discussion_board_memberusers and discussion_board_memberuser_sessions.

The operation will return a single IDiscussionBoardMemberuserSession DTO that mirrors the fields defined on the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions model, such as identifiers, foreign keys to the owning member user, timestamps for creation and last activity, IP address or user agent fields if present in the schema, and any status flags that indicate whether the session is still active. Because this is an administrative inspection API, it is restricted to adminUser actors and never exposed as a self-service session API to end users.

Implementers must enforce that the session returned belongs to the specified member user, using a composite lookup on memberUserId and sessionId or an equivalent constraint derived from the schema. If no matching session exists, a 404-style error should be returned. No mutation of the underlying session record occurs as part of this call.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a single member user's session from the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions table for administrative review.

This operation reads a specific session that belongs to a member user, identified by the path parameters memberUserId and sessionId. It is backed by the discussion_board_memberuser_sessions Prisma model, which stores per-session data for authenticated member accounts, such as the associated member user reference, creation and last-activity timestamps, and any other fields defined in the schema to describe the session context. The API ensures that the requested session is actually associated with the given member user, preventing cross-user leakage of session data.

From a security and authorization perspective, this endpoint is intended only for administrative actors who need to inspect an individual session for debugging, security investigation, or compliance checks. It must not be used as part of regular user login or logout flows, and it does not create, update, or delete any sessions. Implementations should ensure that only appropriate adminUser roles can call this endpoint, and that sensitive fields are handled in accordance with the discussion board's security and privacy requirements.

Error handling should cover scenarios where either the member user does not exist, the session does not exist for the given user, or the caller lacks sufficient authorization. In such cases, the service should respond with clear error semantics consistent with the platform's conventions while avoiding leaking sensitive existence information to unauthorized actors.
